title: Ford Beats Q3 Estimates and Narrows Guidance, but Its EV Losses Keep Growing
dek: Ford's third-quarter profit beat expectations and the bottom of its 2026 profit guidance rose, though Model e is still forecast to lose about $4 billion this year.
author: Meridian Newsroom

image.alt: Electric cars plugged into public charging points

keyPoints: Ford reported third-quarter adjusted earnings of 49 cents a share against roughly 40 cents expected, and adjusted EBIT of $2.66 billion against $2.38 billion expected, according to CNBC and Yahoo Finance.
Automotive revenue of $46.08 billion slightly missed the $46.24 billion estimate.
Ford raised the low end of its 2026 adjusted EBIT guidance to $10.5 billion, for a range of $10.5 billion to $11 billion, and kept adjusted free cash flow guidance at $6 billion to $7 billion.
Model e lost $1.06 billion in the quarter on $1.2 billion of revenue, and Ford still projects a $4 billion loss for the segment in 2026.
body:
Ford Motor beat third-quarter profit expectations on Wednesday, but the report kept the spotlight on the cost of its electric-vehicle push. The company tightened the low end of its full-year profit forecast and said it expects 2027 earnings to be roughly in line with 2026.

## The quarter

Adjusted earnings were 49 cents a share, above the roughly 40 cents analysts expected, according to CNBC. Adjusted earnings before interest and taxes came in at $2.66 billion, compared with $2.38 billion in estimates. Automotive revenue of $46.08 billion was just short of expectations. Ford said adjusted free cash flow for the quarter was $4.7 billion, about $2 billion more than analysts anticipated, according to StreetAccount figures cited by CNBC.

## Guidance and the EV drag

Ford now sees 2026 adjusted EBIT of $10.5 billion to $11 billion, up from a previous $10 billion to $11 billion range. The company's Model e electric-vehicle unit posted a $1.06 billion loss on $1.2 billion of revenue. Ford still expects Model e to lose another $4 billion over the rest of 2026, with extra spending on its Universal EV platform weighing on the second half.

CFO Sherry House told reporters that commodity headwinds are approaching $2.5 billion year over year and that chip prices are likely to rise, more significantly in 2027. Ford also cited a $1 billion benefit from material and warranty cost reductions.

## Production issues

Production disruptions were a recurring theme. Ford has been working to restore output of its F-Series pickups after supplier problems, and Reuters reported that the company idled crews at its Dearborn Truck Plant for nearly a week in September because of a supply problem. Ford called that a short-term supplier issue unrelated to aluminum.

What to watch next is whether the commodity and chip cost increases outpace the warranty savings Ford is promising, and whether Model e losses narrow once the platform spending peaks.

marketImpact.summary: A profit beat and a slightly higher guidance floor support Ford's core business, but the 2027 outlook, rising commodity and chip costs, and a $4 billion EV loss keep the stock's direction uncertain.

tickers.rationale: Earnings and cash flow beat expectations and guidance firmed at the low end, but management flagged rising commodity and chip costs and a 2027 profit outlook only in line with 2026.
Ford's commentary on commodity and chip inflation and EV losses is a read-through for GM, which narrowed its own 2026 guidance last week.

catalysts.event: Regular-session reaction to Ford's third-quarter results

sources.title: Ford reports Q3 earnings beat, tightens lower end of profit forecast but sees $4 billion in EV losses for year
